issue_title: Performance regression on 3 pages: TBT spike site-wide + /projects/screenshot-to-primevue hits 75 (LCP 4.8 s)
issue_body:
# Performance regression — TBT spike site-wide + worsening LCP on /projects/screenshot-to-primevue

Audited: **2026-10-06T15:09:01.780Z**

## Affected pages

| Page | Perf (prev → now) | LCP (prev → now) | TBT (prev → now) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 92 → **81** 🔴 | 3274 ms → 3781 ms | 46 ms → **269 ms** |
| `/projects/note-structurer` | 85 → **79** 🔴 | 3907 ms → 4371 ms | 82 ms → **194 ms** |
| `/projects/screenshot-to-primevue` | 81 → **75** 🔴 | 4320 ms → **4817 ms** | 73 ms → **206 ms** |
| `/about` | 91 → 89 ⚠️ | 3319 ms → 3346 ms | 31 ms → 124 ms |
| `/projects` | 90 → 88 ⚠️ | 3317 ms → 3371 ms | 68 ms → 170 ms |

## Root cause hypothesis
TBT has spiked dramatically (3–6×) across **all five pages** in a single cycle, strongly suggesting a newly introduced or un-deferred JavaScript bundle is blocking the main thread globally. This is not measurement noise — the pattern is consistent across every page.

LCP has also degraded across the board, likely as a secondary effect of main-thread blocking delaying resource fetches.

## Recommended fixes
1. **Audit recent JS changes** — check any new scripts added since the last deploy; a synchronous third-party script (analytics, chat widget, etc.) is the most likely culprit.
2. **Defer or async all non-critical scripts** — ensure no render-blocking JS runs before LCP.
3. **Code-split** any new bundles, particularly on `/projects/screenshot-to-primevue` where LCP is now 4.8 s.
4. **Add `fetchpriority="high"`** to the LCP element on `/projects/screenshot-to-primevue` to partially mitigate the LCP issue regardless of TBT.

## Visual status
All pages are visually intact on desktop and mobile — no layout breakage, overflow, missing sections, or contrast issues detected. This is a pure performance regression.
